description: 3rd connection. 2nd connection's RUNSQL got past the argument-name validation (DATABASE_FILE_TYPE removal worked, and the MONMSG fix let the wrapper reach DONE gracefully this time) but hit a NEW error: 'Conversion error on variable or parameter *N.' Two suspected causes, both fixed here as a single combined attempt (no primary source to isolate which one is real, so testing both changes together - if this also fails, GENERATE_SQL's exact signature will be treated as genuinely unconfirmable without IBM's own online docs and 08-06's design will fall back to a documented, honest 'general knowledge, unconfirmed' framing rather than further blind guessing): (1) DATABASE_SOURCE_FILE_NAME was passed as 'QTEMP/QSQLTEMP' - a slash-separated library-qualified path crammed into what is very likely a plain NAME-type parameter (max 10 chars, no special characters) - changed to plain 'QSQLTEMP' (relying on QTEMP being the default/current-library target, unconfirmed). (2) CREATE_OR_REPLACE_OPTION was passed as the quoted CHAR string '1' - if the real parameter type is INTEGER, a quoted string would cause exactly this class of conversion error - changed to the unquoted numeric literal 1.

steps.label: GENSQL
steps.cmd:
RUNSQL SQL('CALL QSYS2.GENERATE_SQL(DATABASE_OBJECT_NAME => ''TOKUIM'', DATABASE_OBJECT_LIBRARY_NAME => ''&LIB'', DATABASE_SOURCE_FILE_NAME => ''QSQLTEMP'', DATABASE_OBJECT_TYPE => ''*FILE'', CREATE_OR_REPLACE_OPTION => 1)') COMMIT(*NONE)
MONMSG MSGID(CPF0000 SQL0000) EXEC(GOTO CMDLBL(ORIGLVLID))
DSPFD FILE(QTEMP/QSQLTEMP) TYPE(*MBRLIST) OUTPUT(*PRINT)
